questions.q: What are the three parts of a strong resume bullet in the pattern taught here?
questions.explain: A bullet states what you did (action), how you know it mattered (metric) and what you used (tool).

questions.q: Why is a metric like '0.85 accuracy' weak on its own?
options: Accuracy can never be reported on a resume
It has no baseline, so the reader cannot tell if it is good
questions.explain: A number needs a comparison, such as random guessing or a simple baseline, before it means anything.

questions.q: Your capstone used a fictional dataset. What should the resume do?
options: Say so briefly, for example 'capstone project, fictional dataset'
Hide it, since it looks less real
Present the results as a real company's outcomes
questions.explain: Being honest costs nothing and protects you when interviewers ask about each line.

questions.q: Which is the best use of a LinkedIn headline for a job seeker?
options: Role, core searchable skills and one proof point
questions.explain: Recruiters search on keywords, so the headline should carry the role and skills plus a concrete proof point.

questions.q: How long should a resume generally be at this career stage, and what should career changers consider putting first?
options: One page, with projects first if experience is not in data
questions.explain: One page is the common guidance, and projects can lead when prior experience is in another field.
